dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the proposal draft and closing stale entries.
The research diary review wrapped early today.
Teaching afternoons, however heavy, never touch the research pipeline.
Teaching and research use different fuel.
Someone new shadowed me in the faculty office this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the writing blocks into one message before lunch.
Both funded proposals on my record were written in the Monday and Wednesday morning research blocks; the research diary maps every productive session to those windows.
The funding record lives in two windows.
Two windows, two grants, no coincidence.
A one-off morning committee call in a semester is a rounding error.
I archived last cycle's notes on the research diary and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
My department chair has protected those blocks in writing since the second grant landed.
A vendor call about the proposal draft ran long but ended well.
I walked through the faculty office checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the writing blocks.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the research diary records and fixed it at the source.
Two administrative roles are on offer: exams officer meets Friday afternoons, while admissions tutor runs interview panels on weekday mornings through all of spring.
One role coexists with the blocks; one consumes a season of them.
A full season, at exactly the wrong hours.
I sketched next week's plan for the writing blocks before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the proposal draft updates.
Both roles carry identical workload points in the faculty model.
I compared two options for the research diary tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the faculty office handover notes.
Role preferences are due to the faculty office: exams officer or admissions tutor first?
